title: VegasInsider Picks Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Worth It?
description: VegasInsider Premium review, checked 7 Nov 2026: plan prices, the no refund policy, what the expert records show and leave out, and what users report.
dek: A long running odds site, owned by Better Collective since 2019, that sells one subscription to every pick from its roster of experts for $19.99 a month or $119.99 a year. VegasInsider grades its own experts and shows leaderboards, but we could not open a full pick log without paying, and the subscription has no refunds.

short_answer: VegasInsider is a real, well known betting media site. Its terms name Better Collective USA, Inc. as the operator, its prices are posted, and its experts are named. In that sense the Premium subscription is legitimate.

Whether the picks make money is a separate question. VegasInsider grades its own experts at $100 per pick and posts leaderboards, such as Mark Franco at 578-456 (56%) this year. Those are graded by the seller, not by a third party, and the full pick by pick log was not open to us without a subscription. The free picks pages show records like "1-0 NFL Last 3 Days", which tell you almost nothing.

Treat VegasInsider Premium as a cheap bundle of opinions from a seller that also earns from sportsbook signups. If you try it, start with the shortest plan, record every pick with the line and the time you saw it, and remember the plan renews automatically and is not refundable.

guarantee: There is no guarantee. The refund policy says there is "a no refund policy on Vegas Insider Premium monthly or annual subscriptions" and that "refunds will not be provided due to poor predictive performance." The only refunds it describes are for unauthorized or fraudulent card charges, reviewed case by case. It does end by saying customers who feel entitled to a refund can contact the company.

Plans renew on their own. The Why Buy page says "all subscriptions will be automatically billed at the end of your product, either monthly or annually," and the 3 Day Pass says it continues at $19.99 per month. A buyer who only wants a short trial needs to cancel before the pass ends. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered.

claims_note: VegasInsider does more than most pick sellers here. The Why Buy page says it grades every expert at one unit ($100) per pick, does not let experts inflate records with multi unit plays, shows the pick, the publish time and the odds, and requires picks to post at least one hour before the game. Those are good rules. But the grading is done by the company that sells the picks, and the full logs were not open to us without paying.

The leaderboard shows only the top four names per board. A buyer sees the leaders, not the experts who are losing. The profile highlights are titles picked from past seasons, and Stephen Nover's profile says it covers results "heading into 2021", so it is several years old. The free picks pages show records over the last 3 or 7 days, such as 1-0 or 2-0, which are too short to mean anything.
record: What is independently verifiable: nothing we could find. No third party grades the VegasInsider experts, and we found no contest results or regulator records for them. One profile claim points to an outside contest: Mark Franco's bio says he finished fifth in the 2003 Hilton SuperContest at 76-57. We did not check that against the contest's own records.

What is the seller's own record keeping: the Expert Records leaderboards, graded by VegasInsider at $100 per pick. On 7 Nov 2026 the all sports current year board showed Mark Franco at 578-456 (56%) and Stephen Nover at 701-629 (53%). These are full counts, not streaks, which is better than most sellers offer, but we could not open the pick by pick log behind them, so we could not check the prices, the post times or the losing experts left off the board.
What is marketing: the short records shown next to free picks, the season titles on each profile, and the testimonials on the Premium page.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no VegasInsider expert is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how these experts perform.
our_data.context: For scale: VegasInsider says a handicapper needs to be right 55% of the time. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on VegasInsider Premium is thin. The largest sample is the iPhone app rating, which covers the whole app, not just the picks. We found no Reddit thread or forum discussion of the Premium picks. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: Forum bettors talk about VegasInsider as an odds and data site, not as a picks seller. In 2022, Sportsbook Review and Covers members complained that a redesign made the odds pages harder to use and more crowded with ads, and one claimed, without evidence, that its betting percentage data had been shaped by sponsor sportsbooks. We found no buyer describing the paid Premium picks.
The VegasInsider Betting Tips iPhone app showed 4.7 out of 5 from 2.3K ratings. The rating covers odds, news and other app features, so it says little about whether the paid picks win.
An App Store reviewer said sign ups in the app happen with one touch and no confirmation, said this had cost him $40, and praised the content otherwise.
Another App Store reviewer said the app used to be his go to source for consensus data and complained that consensus numbers now sit behind a paywall, though he accepted paying for picks.
The Premium page shows three testimonials from "VIP Subscribers" identified by first name and state. They are chosen by VegasInsider, so they cannot tell you what a typical buyer experiences.
We found no Reddit thread, BBB profile we could confirm, or TheRX, Covers or SBR forum discussion about VegasInsider Premium picks.

conflicts: VegasInsider earns from the betting companies it promotes. Its affiliate disclosure says "we may collect a share of sales or other compensation from the company links provided on this Website." A 2019 Gambling Insider report on the purchase by Better Collective said the new owner would change the site's model from subscription and advertising "to affiliate marketing and lead generation."

The picks sit beside those offers. The NFL free picks page links to a BetMGM bonus code page, which on 7 Nov 2026 promoted code VIBONUS. The site menus carry promo code pages for sportsbooks, prediction markets, casinos and sweepstakes casinos. Each page footer says the site contains commercial content and links the disclosure.
The iPhone app lists RotoGrinders as developer and Rical LLC as seller, not VegasInsider.
strengths: A named corporate operator, posted prices and published refund and terms pages.
Clear grading rules on paper: one unit ($100) per pick, no multi unit padding, picks posted at least an hour before the game, per the Why Buy page.
Leaderboards show full won and lost counts for the leaders, not just hot streaks.
Low price for access to every expert, with a $4.99 short pass to try it.
concerns: No refunds on monthly or annual plans, and plans renew automatically. The $4.99 pass rolls into $19.99 a month.
Records are graded by the seller. The pick by pick log was not open to us without paying, and the boards show only the top names.
The site earns from sportsbook signups and promo codes placed next to its picks.
Prices differ between the Premium page, the Why Buy page and the iPhone app.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: Yes in the narrow sense: VegasInsider is a real media business operated by Better Collective USA, with posted prices and named experts. We could not verify that its experts win over time, because the records are graded by VegasInsider and the full logs were not open to us.
How much does VegasInsider Premium cost?
On 7 Nov 2026 the Premium page listed $19.99 a month, $119.99 a year, or a 3 Day Pass for $4.99 that then bills $19.99 per month. The refund policy says monthly and annual plans are not refundable.
Do VegasInsider experts have a verified record?

Not independently. VegasInsider grades its own experts at $100 per pick and posts leaderboards, such as Mark Franco at 578-456 (56%) this year, but no third party checks them and we could not open the pick by pick log without paying.

For the price you get every pick and write up from the whole roster, plus betting trends. What is unproven is whether following any expert makes money after the -110 juice, so a record you keep yourself is the only way to judge it, and the plan will not be refunded if the picks lose.
